state:
Goal `core-regex-and-1-more`. `Core\Regex::compile`, `match`, `matchAll` and `matches` owe
nothing, and `Core\Regex` has its class card. The cards of `matchAll` and `matches` are in the plain
voice. `replace`, `replaceWith`, `split` and `quote` still owe every proof, and their cards in
`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs` are still in the old voice. A pattern with 5000 groups stops with the
memory-limit `FATAL` under every member that compiles through `compiled_prepared`, including
`matches`, which never reads a group. `Core\Regex\Match` and `Core\Regex\Pattern` are still listed in
`CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD` in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs`.

items.text: **`Core\Regex::replace`** — owes about, examples, hostile, perf and a Rust test with `// covers: Core\Regex::replace` (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). Rewrite `REPLACE_DOC` in the plain voice the way `MATCH_DOC` reads. The attack can try a replacement that expands `$1` into a very large text many times. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs:318` `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs:1714`

**`Core\Regex::replaceWith`** — the same proofs, with `// covers: Core\Regex::replaceWith`; its callback is a real closure, and the playbook's `closure_of` bullet is how a Rust test builds one. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs:1804`

**`Core\Regex::split` and `Core\Regex::quote`** — the same proofs each; `quote`'s attack feeds every special character and a very long text. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs:1897` `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs:1950`

**Record the rows** — `bun nv proofs --record-perf --only 'Core\Regex'` after the last edit to `regex.rs`, since every member's row goes stale when that file moves; `bun nv reference --no-examples` after any card edit. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs:213`

backlog: `Core\Regex::matches` allocates about twice a call on a cached pattern; `data/gaps/nvs-stdlib/regex-matches-allocates-on-every-call.json` owns it, and its bench carries the gap marker.
`Core\Regex\Match` and `Core\Regex\Pattern` owe class cards and every member proof; `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs:5283` lists them (`rule:core-api/reference-card`).
`Core\Regex::matches` prices a capture table it never fills, so a many-groups pattern is refused there too; that is the safe side, and `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/regex.rs`'s `search_cost` owns it.
